targetText: " "The rate of interest depends 1) on the rate of profit; 2) on the proportion in which the entire profit is divided between the lender and borrower.
explanation: The rate of profit ($p/C$) measures surplus value relative to total invested capital (constant plus variable), whereas the rate of surplus value ($s/v$) measures exploitation relative to labor costs alone.

targetText: [5] However, the rate of interest also has a tendency to fall quite independently of the fluctuations in the rate of profit.
explanation: The tendential fall of the rate of profit occurs because technological progress increases constant capital faster than living labor power, shrinking the relative source of surplus value.

targetText: The development of the credit system and the attendant ever-growing control of industrialists and merchants over the money savings of all classes of society that is effected through the bankers, and the progressive concentration of these savings in amounts which can serve as money-capital, must also depress the rate of interest.
explanation: Commercial or merchant capital doesn’t create new surplus value directly, but collects a share of total social profit by speeding up the circulation and sale of goods.
